title: install.py transaction engine and Claude Code projection

completion.statement: install.py (stdlib) transaction engine and the Claude Code projection are implemented: in-memory write plan with before/after hashes, conflict refusal with zero writes (unowned collisions, modified managed files, tampered block markers, symlink escapes, malformed settings), --allow-overwrite with 0700/0600 backups, a bounded fcntl install lock with before-hash rechecks, atomic writes with rollback, and the ownership manifest written last against schemas/installation.schema.json. Settings merges preserve all user keys/hooks/permissions; CLAUDE.md gets a managed block; .gitignore gains only volatile entries and never the committed context home (nothing under .software-factory/context/ is written or listed in the manifest). Dry-run writes nothing and spawns nothing; a second install is a byte-level no-op; Git and HOME configs are never touched; no active.json is created. The Claude projection mirrors the 11 skills into .claude/skills with argument-hint on all and disable-model-invocation on the six entry/admin skills, copies the 11 role agents, and merges SessionStart/PreCompact hook commands with stderr merged into stdout (2>&1).

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (338 tests OK after board projection rebuild)
